transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~73 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Dante Ruiz (Redwood Solutions Architect), Ken Park (Sable Tech - InfoSec), Maya Lopez (Sable Tech - Cloud Eng), Tara Singh (Sable Tech - Compliance)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Redwood walked through the Trust Center access model, SOC 2 / ISO artifacts available, RBAC/SSO and SCIM provisioning options, audit log retention and export, and KMS / BYOK integration story. Customer requested read-only access to the evidence portal, a controls mapping spreadsheet, and confirmation of data residency / log shipping for their EU workload. Several minor transcription errors expected (acronyms, product names).

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Ken (Sable): Ken here.
[00:10] Maya: Maya on the call.
[00:12] Tara: Tara here.
[00:15] Alex: Great. Priya and Dante also with me from Redwood. Today we planned a posture review — SOC 2 / ISO artifacts, trust center access, RBAC/SSO, audit logging, KMS. We should also capture any gaps for your auditors.
[00:32] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll take the technical side — how Trust Center is organized, what we share, and the RBAC model. Dante will cover controls mapping and evidence exports.
[00:40] Ken: Sounds good. Our timeline is tight — our external audit is scheduled for late Jan, so we're trying to get a clean mapping by end of year.
[00:50] Tara: and we need role-based access to the evidence portal for our auditors and internal control owners.
[00:55] Priya: Understood — we have read-only roles, and we can do scoped access to specific reports and evidence. I'll walk through that in a moment.

[01:20] Priya: Ok I'm sharing my screen — Trust Center home (link: https://trustcenter.redwood.ai/sabletech — note: sample link only). Top left you see Reports, Evidence, Audit Logs, and Integrations.
[01:38] Maya: That sample link, is that accessible for us now?
[01:41] Priya: Not yet — I'll request a tenant-level read-only grant for ken@ and tara@ after this call, and you'll get an invite. It takes a couple minutes to provision.
[01:50] Ken: We need the auditors to be able to download SOC 2 artifacts. Is there a redacted copy you can share now?
[01:57] Alex: Yes, we'll send the redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF and ISO 27001 certificate post-call. That's standard.

[02:16] Priya: On the Reports tab — you can see our SOC 2 Type II report, system description, policy snapshots, and penetration test summary. For ISO 27001 we have the certification and the scope document. The evidence tab contains control-specific artifacts — logs, config screenshots, and policy attestations.
[02:40] Ken: How do you handle evidence that contains customer data? Example: audit logs with IPs or userIDs.
[02:47] Priya: Good question — we redact PII in the shared artifacts by default. For audit logs, the exported bundles have options to anonymize or mask fields. We can also ship logs to your SIEM if you prefer to keep raw data in your environment.

[03:10] Dante: I'll jump to controls mapping — we maintain a spreadsheet mapping Redwood's controls to common frameworks (SOC 2 CC, ISO A.5-A.18) and we can add a column mapping to Sable Tech's internal control IDs. That helps your auditors see coverage.
[03:28] Tara: Perfect. Can you add control owners and evidence file names in that sheet?
[03:34] Dante: Yep. We'll include evidence filenames, the last updated timestamp, and the Redactor used.

[03:50] [Speaker 3]: (mumble) question about KMS...
[03:55] Priya: The KMS story: we support customer-managed keys for encryption at rest (BYOK/HSM). You can integrate via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or bring an external HSM. We also have envelope encryption; the platform uses service keys wrapped by your KMS.
[04:20] Maya: For BYOK, do you rotate keys automatically or is that manual?
[04:24] Priya: We don't rotate customer-managed keys — rotation is controlled by the customer in their KMS. For platform keys we rotate on a schedule and will document material rotation events in the Trust Center.

[04:48] Ken: Are audit logs available in raw form and what's the retention?
[04:52] Priya: Default retention for audit logs in hosted is 365 days, with add-on options for longer retention. We can also stream logs to your SIEM via secure syslog/HTTPS. The logs include request metadata, model variant, route, and token counts, but we mask prompt/response payloads unless you opt-in and sign a data-sharing contract.
[05:20] Ken: Ok we need 2 years of logs for some controls. Is that a paid retention add-on?
[05:26] Alex: Yes, extended retention is an add-on; we can size it and include in a Dedicated/Private commit too. We'll estimate cost in the follow-up.

[05:45] Priya: About RBAC and SSO: we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC for single sign-on, SCIM for provisioning. Roles can be tenant-admin, auditor-readonly, devops, and operator. Each role has scoped permissions — for example auditor-readonly cannot download raw PII-laden evidence.
[06:10] Maya: Do you support granular permissions per model or per route?
[06:13] Priya: We currently support per-resource RBAC for Projects and Routes. Per-model permissioning is on the roadmap; we can add a note in the controls mapping that route-level scoping applies today.

[06:35] Tara: For SCIM provisioning, do you support attribute mapping for job title / control owner?
[06:40] Priya: Yes, SCIM allows us to map groups to RBAC roles and push attributes. We usually map group membership and email. If you need custom attributes, we can discuss a mapping plan in the next tech sync.

[07:05] Ken: What's the SSO session lifetime? We require maximum session window of 12 hours.
[07:11] Priya: Session timeout is configurable per tenant. We default to 8 hours but can set to 12 or lower per your policy.

[07:30] [00:07:30] Dante: On controls evidence exports — we can generate a zipped evidence package per control that includes annotated screenshots, log snippets, and config manifests. Each artifact is time-stamped and the export has a generated manifest.csv for auditor ingestion.
[07:52] Ken: Nice. For pen test reports, do you provide full reports or summaries?
[07:57] Priya: We provide a redacted pen test report; full reports are shared under NDA for enterprise customers. If your auditor needs full details, we have a standard process to share under a controlled access pattern.

[08:20] Maya: Data residency — we have EU workloads that must not leave eu-west-1. How do you ensure control plane telemetry doesn't cross borders?
[08:28] Priya: For Private and Dedicated customers we offer region-scoped deployments. For hosted, we logically isolate data and can provide EU-only processing and storage guarantees for customer data. Certain telemetry (anonymized usage metrics) might be aggregated globally, but we can flag critical logs to remain in-region. We'll capture specifics in the controls mapping doc.

[08:55] Ken: Can you export the evidence into our S3 bucket?
[08:59] Dante: Yes, we support secure S3 exports (signed URL or cross-account role) for evidence bundles. We do checksum verifications and include a manifest.

[09:20] [09:20] Tara: A quick question on encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between services?
[09:26] Priya: We use TLS 1.2+ for all external connections and support mTLS for private deployments. For hosted, mutual TLS to our public APIs isn't generally offered, but we can discuss a dedicated gateway if you need mTLS from your side.

[09:50] Ken: Regarding access logs for admin actions — do you retain who invoked rollouts or config changes?
[09:56] Priya: Yes — admin audit trails include user, action, timestamp, and originating IP. We surface these in the Audit Logs UI and you can export them.

[10:18] [10:18] Maya: For the SIEM integration, do you have structured log schema docs?
[10:23] Priya: Yes we have a Logs Schema doc (JSON schema) that we'll share. It includes fields like: tenant_id, request_id, route, model, user_id (if enabled), masked_payload_indicator, and event_type.

[11:00] Ken: How does the controls mapping handle shared responsibilities for infrastructure (e.g., underlying cloud provider)?
[11:06] Dante: We annotate each control with responsibility: Redwood, Cloud Provider, or Customer. The mapping has a color-coded column. For example, physical security is cloud provider, but access control for the Redwood console is our responsibility.

[11:30] Tara: Do you track changes to policies and configurations for evidence lineage?
[11:34] Priya: Yes — policy changes are versioned. Evidence entries have a provenance record: created_by, created_at, and change history.

[12:02] [12:02] Ken: One of the auditors asked about SLA breach reporting — if there's an incident, how do you provide evidence for incident response timelines?
[12:12] Alex: We provide incident timelines, post-incident reports, and root-cause analysis artifacts in the Trust Center for customers with the appropriate support tier. We can also provide redacted timelines under NDA.

[12:40] Priya: Quick demo of granting auditor access: navigate to Tenant -> Users -> Invite, enter email, assign role auditor-readonly, optionally scope to Projects "Payments" and "EU-Workload." You can check the "disable downloads" box if you need download prevention.
[13:05] Maya: Can the auditor still view logs if downloads disabled?
[13:09] Priya: They can view summarized logs; download is blocked. Raw exports require explicit permission.

[13:30] [13:30] Ken: About keys — if we want HSM-backed keys with an external HSM vendor, is there a recommended configuration?
[13:38] Dante: We recommend using cloud KMS with HSM-backed key material (e.g., AWS KMS with custom key store or Azure Managed HSM). For external HSMs, we support a gateway model or customer-hosted key wrap service, though that may require a Dedicated deployment.

[14:05] Tara: For our controls, auditors like to see proof of emp... (mumble) separation of duties. How do you show that?
[14:12] Priya: Separation is enforced via RBAC and approval workflows for sensitive actions. We can provide screenshots of role definitions and the approval logs showing two-person approval for config changes.

[14:35] [14:35] Maya: Any limitations around exporting model input/output for troubleshooting?
[14:40] Priya: We generally mask inputs/outputs. For troubleshooting we can enable a temporary, time-limited debug export with explicit consent and extra controls. These exports are kept outside the standard retention and require an approval record.

[15:00] [15:00] Ken: Ok, on the controls spreadsheet — can you map our control IDs like SBL-AC-01 to Redwood controls?
[15:06] Dante: Absolutely. We'll add a column for Sable control IDs and populate the mapping with evidence filename links.

[15:30] Tara: Can you also surface the date of last evidence refresh? Auditors keep asking that.
[15:34] Dante: We'll include last_refreshed and version columns.

[16:00] [16:00] Priya: A couple of edge points: for on-prem/private deployments we can provide complete source-of-truth logs and mTLS, and bring-your-own-hsm is fully supported. For hosted we provide strong logical separation and contractual assurances.
[16:24] Ken: If we go Dedicated, can we get longer default log retention without add-on costs?
[16:30] Alex: Typically Dedicated contracts include a retention baseline that we can negotiate — we'll put proposed numbers in the follow-up.

[17:00] [17:00] Maya: For the Trust Center, is there an API to pull evidence programmatically?
[17:04] Priya: Yes, there's an Evidence API with token-based auth that returns a manifest and signed URLs. We'll include API docs link in the follow-up.

[17:30] Ken: Any recent audit findings we should be aware of?
[17:33] Alex: Nothing material — in the last audit there were some recommended improvements around retention labeling and a minor control narrative tweak. We addressed both and updated the Trust Center.

[18:05] [18:05] Tara: On privacy, do you provide a DPA and data processing addendum?
[18:10] Alex: Yes — standard DPA and SCCs for EU customers; we can attach the executed copy to the Trust Center or directly to your legal team.

[18:40] Priya: Quick demo: showing an evidence item — named "access_log_2025-10-03.json.gz.redacted" — metadata visible: created_by, control_id, related_audit, sha256. There's a download box with an expiration.

[19:05] Maya: The redaction looks automated — can you customize redaction rules?
[19:09] Priya: We offer templates (PII, IP-only, none). For enterprise we can do custom redaction policies.

[19:40] [19:40] Ken: About control owners — can we assign our internal owners so your evidence flags review-needed?
[19:46] Dante: Yes, control entries can include a customer_owner field and we can trigger reminders to those owners when evidence ages out.

[20:10] Tara: Do you keep an immutable audit trail for evidence changes?
[20:14] Priya: We store an append-only changelog for evidence metadata with hashes of artifacts to prove immutability.

[20:40] [20:40] Ken: For incident reporting to our team — do you have SLA for notification?
[20:44] Alex: We have defined escalation and notification SLAs depending on severity. Critical incidents have 60-minute customer-notify targets for enterprise. We'll include the exact SLA table in the follow-up.

[21:10] [21:10] Maya: Anything about third-party subprocessor list?
[21:14] Priya: We publish a subprocessors list in the Trust Center and send 30-day notices for material changes.

[21:40] Ken: Ok let's pivot to next steps and concrete asks so we can close on tasks.
[21:46] Alex: Recap: we'll share the redacted SOC 2 and ISO cert, Priya will provision Trust Center read-only for your auditors, Dante will deliver controls mapping spreadsheet, and Maya will share retention and SIEM details. Anything else?
[22:05] Tara: Please include the logs schema and API docs as well.
[22:09] Priya: Will do.

[22:30] [22:30] Ken: One last question — are there any known limitations that would block our auditors from verifying encryption-in-use and key ownership?
[22:36] Dante: No blockers — for BYOK we can demonstrate key lineage and wrap/unwrap evidence, and for managed keys we provide detailed KMS logs.

[23:00] [23:00] Alex: Great. We'll follow up with the package. If you want to run a short trust center walkthrough with your auditors present we can schedule a 30-minute session next week.
[23:15] Maya: Let's do that — maybe Wednesday morning.
[23:18] Ken: Works for me.

[23:30] [23:30] (wrap-up chatter, scheduling tentative times)

[24:00] Post-call notes (auto): Attendees expressed interest in Dedicated vs Hosted for stricter residency. Primary asks: read-only Trust Center access, controls mapping spreadsheet, SOC2/ISO artifacts, SIEM integration details, KMS/BYOK confirmation.

End transcript.
